content.content:
---
name: render-marp-decks-to-pdf
description: make PDFs of Marp slide decks (slides.md) next to each deck and check that no slide overflows its page; fix overflow without changing slide text
---
1. Find a browser: `ls /opt/pw-browsers/*/chrome-linux/chrome` (or chromium/chrome on PATH); export CHROME_PATH to it. Marp CLI runs via `npx --yes @marp-team/marp-cli`, no install needed.
2. For each deck: `npx --yes @marp-team/marp-cli <dir>/slides.md --pdf -o <dir>/slides.pdf --allow-local-files`. Check `pdfinfo` page count equals the number of slides.
3. Check overflow in the PDF itself (not by measuring the HTML export, which lays code blocks out differently and gives wrong answers): `pdftotext -bbox <pdf> -`, per page ignore the page number (bottom right) and header; flag any word with yMax > 482pt or xMax > 901pt (page is 960x540pt, Marp padding 78px). Also pixel-check with `pdftoppm -r 48 -gray` for ink in the bottom band, right and left margins (tables and boxes).
4. Validate the checker on the pre-fix deck (render an original copy from git) so you know it catches overflow.
5. Fix only with a `<style scoped>` block at the top of the slide (`section { font-size: 24px; }`, `table { font-size: 0.7em; }`, for code set `pre { font-size: 0.6em; line-height: 1.25; }`, since pre line height follows the pre, not the code). Never change slide text. Re-render and recheck.
6. Beware: another process may commit work in the repo mid-session; compare against `git show HEAD~N:` rather than assuming HEAD is the original.
7. Note how the PDFs are regenerated in AGENTS.md (creator info), not in reader files.

Five slides overflowed, in two decks. I found them by measuring where the text sat on each page, not by looking at images.

**Which slides**

These are the pre-fix PDF measurements from step 65, with the overflow in points on a 960×540 page. Slide 64 of Lesson 2 is the exception: it overflowed only in the HTML preview, not in the PDF.

| Deck | Slide | Content | Overflow (pre-fix PDF) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Lesson 2 | 22 | the model's request (JSON block) | bottom 537, right 558 |
| Lesson 2 | 38 | `ls -la` | bottom 489, right 692 |
| Lesson 2 | 64 | three tools at once | none in the PDF |
| Lesson 4 | 42 | the four memories (table) | bottom 539, right 888 |
| Lesson 4 | 71 | the choices you make | bottom 528, right 895 |

The other eight decks had no overflowing slides.

**How I found out**

1. **HTML measurement first.** I rendered each deck to HTML and loaded it in headless Chromium through Playwright. A script compared each slide's content against the 1280×720 slide box. It flagged Lesson 2 slides 22, 38 and 64, and Lesson 4 slides 42 and 71.
2. **Text positions in the PDF.** `/tmp/bbox.py` ran `pdftotext -bbox` on each PDF. That gives a bounding box for every word on every page. It flagged any word below y=482pt or right of x=901pt, ignoring the page number and header. I picked those limits to keep Marp's padding margins clear.
3. **Pixel check as a second signal.** I rasterised the pages with `pdftoppm -r 48 -gray` and looked for dark pixels in the bottom band and the side margins. It came back clean on the fixed decks.
4. **Testing the checker.** My first "original" was `git show HEAD`, but a commit had landed mid-session that already contained my fixes. That made the pixel check read 0 and look blind. I then rendered `HEAD~1` and ran the bbox check on it. It flagged the four PDF slides above, so the bbox check does catch real overflow. It also showed that slide 64 only overflowed in the HTML preview.
5. **Fix and recheck.** I added a `<style scoped>` block to each slide that only shrinks the font, so no text changed. I re-rendered all ten decks, and the bbox and pixel checks passed on every one.

I never saw any slide. The evidence is word coordinates and ink counts, which I trust because the bbox check flagged the pre-fix PDFs and passed the fixed ones.
